current.text: White re-signed with Charlotte for 3 years and 74 million USD.
Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges. White is the projected starting point guard, and the projected starters are White, Knueppel, Miller, Reid and Diabaté.
Dennis Schroder is on the Charlotte roster and is listed on the bench. Charlotte has no backup point guard the team trusts.
The experts see White as the clear starter over Schroder and are not worried about him. Some in the market think they will share minutes, and that is part of why his ADP is low.
Last season he played limited minutes, had several calf injuries and became LaMelo Ball's backup after his trade to Charlotte. None of those factors apply now.
He is projected for about 30 to 32 minutes or more, up from 25 last season.
His usage should dip a little from last season's very high level but stay good, at about 28. One expert sees him as only the third or fourth usage option behind Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller.
Charlotte plans to spread the ball handling and playmaking across White, Knueppel and Miller instead of using one primary creator.
Without Ball and Giddey next to him, he should reach 20 or more points and 5 to 6 assists, possibly 6 to 7 assists.
His FT% drop last season had no real cause, and it is expected to bounce back.
The experts call him underpriced. They would draft him around rank 55 to 75, in the 60s or in rounds 6 to 7. They see a top 75 floor with top 50 upside, and he is the best target on Charlotte.
In an auction mock he went for 13 USD, which the expert called really good value.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes.
Charlotte has 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games. It also has a two-game week in the matchup starting March 1.

durable.text: He is a good scorer and a good three-point shooter, including off the dribble. His FT% is strong.
He is a streaky, inconsistent shooter, and his FG% swings up and down.
His steals and blocks are very poor. His combined stocks are among the worst for a starter.
He is a fine passer but not a pass-first point guard. The experts rate his assist output as modest for the role.
He attacks the paint, finishes at the rim and gets to the free throw line.
Apart from last season's calf injuries, he has been fairly durable over the last four years.

note: The market prices him like a backup: Yahoo value 12 USD, ESPN value 2 USD and Yahoo rank 80. In our league he went for 15 USD last season, and the experts rank him around 55 to 75 now that he starts at point guard. A bid of about 13 to 18 USD looks like good value. He fits builds that want 3PM, FT%, PTS and AST from a guard, but he gives little in steals and blocks, has some turnovers and is slightly below average in FG%, so he pairs well with stocks-heavy bigs. Early in the season, check that he gets 30 or more minutes with Schroder on the bench, gets about 5 to 6 assists while sharing the ball with Knueppel and Miller, and that his FT% returns to the mid 80s or higher.
